story: I worked as a cashier in a supermarket in Abu Dhabi, not in a free zone, from 1 June 2024. On 20 September my manager told me my job ends today. They gave me no notice. My contract says 30 days' notice. My basic salary is 2,000 dirhams and my total salary is 3,000.

output.scope_reason: Private sector worker in mainland Abu Dhabi.
output.facts_summary_en: The worker was employed as a cashier at a supermarket in Abu Dhabi mainland. Employment began on 2024-06-01 and ended on 2026-09-20. The employer terminated the worker without providing notice. The contract stipulates a 30-day notice period. The total monthly salary is 3,000 AED, with a basic salary of 2,000 AED.

issues.finding: The employer terminated the worker without providing the contractually required 30-day notice period, making the worker entitled to a warning allowance.
issues.evidence: The worker stated they were told their job ends immediately on 20 September, despite a 30-day notice period in the contract.

issues.finding: The worker is entitled to an end-of-service gratuity as they have completed more than one year of continuous service.
issues.evidence: The worker has completed 2.31 years of service, which exceeds the one-year requirement for foreign full-time workers.

output.time_limit_note: The case for any rights entitled under this Law shall not be heard after the lapse of two years from the date of work relation termination.
next_steps: File a formal complaint with the Ministry of Human Resources & Emiratisation (MOHRE) to seek an amicable settlement.
Gather your employment contract and any written termination notice provided by the employer.
Prepare copies of your bank statements or payslips to prove your last received wage.
If MOHRE cannot resolve the dispute, request the referral of the case to the competent court.
